subject: CAIQ automated-control-mapping & telemetry evidence SLA request
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@crescentbank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: CrescentBank Security <security@crescentbank.com>, Procurement <procure@crescentbank.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ request and telemetry sample requirements

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick intro call this morning. As mentioned, CrescentBank is running a CSA assessment and we need a CAIQ response that is mapped to our control catalog. Two specific asks from our audit team: 

- A CAIQ-to-control mapping spreadsheet (control IDs mapped to your internal control artifacts).
- Short telemetry samples (redacted) demonstrating runtime isolation, request logging, and retention. Audit needs logs that show prefix caching behavior and KV cache invalidation events.

I attached the CAIQ template the assessor prefers (CrescentBank_CAIQ_Request.pdf). We also want to propose a timeline: submission of mapping by next Thursday, and sample logs uploaded to a pre-authorized GDrive folder within 7 calendar days of mapping delivery. If any of this requires an SLA exception or retention change on Redwood's side, we need to flag that now so our procurement team can prepare paperwork.

Can you confirm who will own the mapping and the telemetry sample handoff?

Best,
Alex Turner
Security Engineering, CrescentBank

Attachment: CrescentBank_CAIQ_Request.pdf (application/pdf, stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@crescentbank.com>, CrescentBank Security <security@crescentbank.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ request and telemetry sample requirements

Thanks Alex — got it.

Marissa / Jordan / David: can one of you lead the CAIQ mapping for CrescentBank? My proposed approach: run the automated CAIQ export from our control registry, then manually annotate ~15 control rows that relate to telemetry/runtime (e.g., LOG-01, ISOL-03, RET-02) and attach example artifacts. Marissa — would you be able to produce the initial mapping spreadsheet and a short playbook for which telemetry samples we can provide without violating PII or tenant isolation?

Notes / constraints:
- Our default log retention is 30 days for request traces and 90 days for aggregated telemetry. The auditor is asking for raw traces — that will require an exception or scoped extraction with redaction.
- We should avoid exposing customer tenant IDs; provide anonymized prefixes and matched event sequences.

Suggested timeline:
- Wed (tomorrow): Marissa shares the mapping proposal (automated + hand-annotated).
- Fri: agree on a scoped list of telemetry traces and upload path.
- Next Thu: final CAIQ spreadsheet delivered to CrescentBank.

I've attached a short proposal workbook to show the export format.

Kimberly Park
Head of Security Programs, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_caiq_mapping_proposal.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@crescentbank.com>, CrescentBank Security <security@crescentbank.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ request and telemetry sample requirements

Kimberly / team — attaching the first pass mapping export + a short guide for telemetry selection. Summary: automated export covers 85% of CAIQ rows; I hand-annotated 18 rows that require runtime evidence (logging, KV cache behavior, deployment isolation). For telemetry, my plan is:

1) Use scoped extraction from the telemetry pipeline for three non-production tenants with synthetic load that reproduce caching and request traces.
2) Redact identifiers and replace them with stable pseudonyms (tenant-A, tenant-B) and include event sequence numbers for traceability.
3) Provide a checksum and time-window for each sample so auditor can correlate steps.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bC-Redwood-Crescent-CAIQ (I put mapping_export_v0.3.xlsx and telemetry_sample_instructions.md there).

Questions for CrescentBank: will a redacted live trace satisfy the auditor, or do you insist on original unredacted windows under a controlled Azure/AWS log share? That determines whether we need a formal SLA retention exception.

Attachments uploaded to the Drive: mapping_export_v0.3.xlsx, telemetry_sample_instructions.md

--
Marissa Cole
Security Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@crescentbank.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 15:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ request and telemetry sample requirements

Kimberly / Alex — quick operational note: if we provide raw traces beyond our default retention window (30 days for request traces), that triggers two things on our side: a temporary retention exception and an internal change ticket for telemetry access (audit log). Both require procurement-level sign-off for data-handling exceptions.

Alex — do you have a procurement contact who can accept a scoped retention exception? We can prepare a DocuSign for a limited purpose (retain traces for 14 extra days, read-only share to CrescentBank auditors). I started a draft DocuSign envelope and saved it under the shared Drive — link below. If Procurement signs, CS/Infra can spin up the scoped extraction and we can upload the redacted traces to the pre-authorized folder.

DocuSign (draft): https://app.docusign.com/prepare/abcdef-telemetry-sla-exception

Jordan Blake
Security Product, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ automated-control-mapping & telemetry evidence SLA request

Alex — thanks for laying out the request. Per the internal review we've put together a mutual action plan below. If CrescentBank procurement can sign the scoped DocuSign exception, Redwood will deliver:

Mutual Action Plan (MAP)
- Today (Thu): Marissa uploads mapping_export_v0.3.xlsx to the shared Drive and flags runtime control rows.
- Fri (within 24 hours): CrescentBank procurement to review and, if acceptable, sign the DocuSign retention exception for the specified time window. DocuSign link (again): https://app.docusign.com/prepare/abcdef-telemetry-sla-exception
- Mon: CS/Infra performs scoped extraction for three synthetic tenants, redacts identifiers, and uploads zipped traces to the Drive folder.
- Thu (next week): Finalized CAIQ spreadsheet with embedded evidence links sent to CrescentBank audit.

Evidence handling notes:
- All telemetry samples will be redacted and labeled with stable pseudonyms (tenant-A/B/C) and checksums.
- We will only grant read-only access to the pre-authorized Drive folder; access logs will be recorded and included in the CAIQ evidence index.
- If CrescentBank requires unredacted traces for legal/regulatory reasons, we will need a separate legal data-share agreement and additional controls.

Action items:
- Alex / Procurement: confirm and sign DocuSign envelope by Fri EOD.
- Marissa: confirm upload (done).
- Jordan / CS: prepare extraction runbook and expected artifact list.
- Kimberly: I will coordinate the CAIQ spreadsheet finalization and send the deliverable once evidence is in place.

Thanks — appreciate the collaboration.

Kimberly Park
Head of Security Programs, Redwood Inference
